successors.note: 'The Idrisids were expelled from their territories and al-Hasan ... were taken as hostages to Cordoba in 974.' The dynasty's last attempt, with Fatimid support, failed in 985. The page names no other heir of the Idrisid lands.

capitals.note: Founded as Medinat Fas in 789 by Idris I; made the seat in 809 by Idris II (infobox: Fez 808-927).

capitals.name: Hajar an-Nasr
capitals.note: Infobox 'Hajar an-Nasar (927-985)'; 'The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco.' The page gives no coordinates; the point is a rough one in the Jbala hills (confidence 1).

correction.text: Volubilis, the first seat, and Tlemcen from 789

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 788-792: Cliopatria's first Idrisid shape begins in 793, but 'Idris I first established himself in 788 at Volubilis ... with the help of local Berber allies' and 'In 789 AD, he captured Tlemcen' from the Sufrite Ifranid Abu Qurra (Idris I page); the Awraba took him in at Volubilis. The page gives the two towns, not a boundary; the 793 shape (all of northern Morocco) is the extent reached by Idris II.

correction.text: the 793 shape plus the Sous, reached by 828

keyframe_review.note: Valid 793-921 with the Sous added: by the end of Idris II's reign (828) 'the realm reached from the Chelif River in modern Algeria to the Sous region in southern Morocco', but Cliopatria's shape (194,486 km2) stops at about 31.3N and 0.0E and has no Sous. The Barghawata and Nekor are outside it (Cliopatria cuts both out); the Idrisid page has 'the principalities of Sijilmasa, Barghawata and Nekor which remained outside their control' in 828, while the Nekor page says Nekor was 'under Idrisid rule' without a date. In 828 the realm was divided among Idris II's brothers (eight statelets) with 'only nominal power' for Muhammad at Fes. The infobox gives 'most of present-day Morocco and parts of present-day western Algeria' with no area.

194,158 km2 for 911-921, essentially the 793 outline. In 917 the Miknasa 'acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes'; Yahya IV was 'deposed in 919 or 921', which ends the Idrisid hold on Fes and the shape in 921.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 925-927: the Idrisid country round Fes under Hassan al-Hajam

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged but valid 925-927 only. Hassan al-Hajam held Fes 925-927 ('Hassan al-Hajam (925-927)'); 'in 927 Musa returned, captured Hassan and killed him, marking the last time the Idrisids held power in Fes'. Cliopatria has no Idrisid shape for 922-925 (its Fatimid row covers Morocco) and the page says nothing on the land between 921 and 925. Repair fx-01 (conflict with fatimid-caliphate, 928 and 936, 552 cells): the keyframe had no years of its own, so the compiler gave it Cliopatria's span 926-935 and kept the whole 194,000 km2 alive through 928 and 936 beside the 928 keyframe (the Rif). The note's years are now explicit: 925-927, until Musa 'returned, captured Hassan and killed him' in 927 (Idrisid Dynasty page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 928-973: after 927 the dynasty holds only the north: 'The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco' (capital 927-985); al-Qasim Gannun rules the north 938-948 'for the Fatimids'; Hasan ibn al-Qasim al-Gannun leads from 954. The page names no boundary; the Rif and the Tangier-Tetouan country stand for the north. Cliopatria's 947 and 970 shapes keep the whole 194,000 km2 for these years.

ledger.note: 788: Idris I establishes himself at Volubilis. 'Idris I first established himself in 788 at Volubilis in present-day Morocco with the help of local Berber allies'; the Awraba made him their imam. Infobox 'Established: 788'.

789: Tlemcen captured. 'In 789 AD, he captured Tlemcen' from the Sufrite Ifranid Abu Qurra; the Tlemcen page has Idris I found the Great Mosque of Agadir there about 790 but lists the Rustamids for 790-798 and the Idrisids for 798-831. The same year he founded Medinat Fas (Fez) per the Idrisid page.

region.text: the 793 outline outside Volubilis and Tlemcen: 'large parts of northern Morocco'

ledger.note: 790-791: the rest of the north. Idris I 'conquered large parts of northern Morocco' (founding Fez, capturing Tlemcen); the page gives no year within his reign 788-791 and names none of the tribes or places (the Zanata, Masmuda, Ghumara and Sanhaja are not on it). Placed at the end of the reign so that Cliopatria's 793 outline is reached; confidence 1.
809: Idris II moves the capital to Fez. 'In 809 moved his seat of government from the Awraba dominated Walili to Fes, where he founded a new settlement named Al-'Aliya.' Infobox: Fez from 808.

region.text: the Sous region of southern Morocco

ledger.note: 828: the Sous is within the realm. 'By the end of his reign, the realm reached from the Chelif River in modern Algeria to the Sous region in southern Morocco.' Idris II died at Fes in 828; the page gives no earlier date for the Sous.

region.text: the Idrisid realm outside Fes, shared among the brothers

ledger.note: 828: the realm is divided. 'The kingdom was divided amongst seven of his brothers, whereby eight Idrisid statelets formed'; Muhammad 'came to rule Fes, with only nominal power over his brothers'; al-Qasim took Tangier, Umar the Rif, Isa the Tamesna coast, Hamza Walili, Ubayd Allah the south, and Muhammad ibn Sulayman Tlemcen. The Idris II page says 'nine principalities ruled by his sons'. Same dynasty, same colour.
917: the Fatimid camp attacks Fes. 'In 917 the Miknasa and its leader Masala ibn Habus, acting on behalf of their Fatimid allies, attacked Fes.'

921: Fes lost. Yahya IV was 'deposed in 919 or 921' and 'succeeded by his cousin Musa ibn Abul 'Afiya', the Fatimid ally; 921 is the later of the two years and matches the end of Cliopatria's 911 shape.
921: the fighting for Fes ends with the deposition of Yahya IV.
925: Hassan al-Hajam holds Fes for the Idrisids ('Hassan al-Hajam (925-927)'), after Fatimid-backed rule since 921.

ledger.note: 927: the last Idrisid hold on Fes ends. 'In 927 Musa returned, captured Hassan and killed him, marking the last time the Idrisids held power in Fes.' Musa was still a Fatimid ally in 927; he 'switched allegiance to the Umayyads of Cordoba in 931'.
927: the family withdraws to Hajar an-Nasr. 'The family took refuge at the fortress of Hajar an-Nasr in northern Morocco'; infobox capital 'Hajar an-Nasar (927-985)'.

wars.name: Idris I's conquests
wars.outcome: Idris I takes Tlemcen in 789 and 'conquered large parts of northern Morocco'; he died in 791, 'allegedly poisoned by the caliph's agents' on the orders of Harun al-Rashid.

wars.name: Fatimid-backed campaigns for Fes
wars.outcome: The Miknasa, for their Fatimid allies, attack Fes in 917; Yahya IV is deposed in 919 or 921; Hassan al-Hajam holds it 925-927 until Musa ibn Abul 'Afiya kills him in 927.

zones.text: northern Morocco: the Rif and the Tangier-Tetouan country, where the family took refuge at Hajar an-Nasr

wars.outcome: Jawhar invades in 958, Ghalib in 973; the Idrisids are expelled and taken to Cordoba in 974; the Umayyads keep northern Morocco.

certainty.note: The pages name towns (Volubilis, Fes, Tlemcen, Tangier) and tribes (Awraba, Sanhaja, Ghumara, Lamta), never frontiers; after 828 the realm is a set of principalities with nominal central power, and after 927 the northern hill country is a refuge.

notes: Cliopatria's Idrisid row is one 194,000 km2 outline for 793-979 with gaps 922-925 and 936-946 where its Fatimid row covers Morocco. The pages opened (five) date: founding 788; Tlemcen 789; Fez 809; division 828; Fatimid-backed attacks from 917; Fes lost 919/921 and regained 925-927; the north as refuge 927-974; expulsion 974. They do not date the Sous, Tadla, Azrou or the Zenata/Maghrawa beyond what is quoted, so the Sous gain is dated by Idris II's death (828) at confidence 2. Conflicts between pages: the Idris II page says nine principalities ruled by sons, the Idrisid page eight statelets for seven brothers; Idris I's arrival in Tangier 789 then Walili (Idris I page) vs established at Volubilis 788 (Idrisid page); the Tlemcen timeline alternates Rustamid and Idrisid rule (Rustamid 790-798, Idrisid 798-831, Rustamid 831-902, Idrisid 902-919) against Idris I's capture in 789; Nekor is 'under Idrisid rule' (Nekor page, undated) but 'outside their control' in 828 (Idrisid page); Fatimid sack of Nekor in 917 and 934 vs Musa's sack in 931. Not drawn: the principalities of 828-836 as separate units (one dynasty, nominal central power), Idrisid control between 836 and 917 (the pages are silent), and the Hammudid branch (Umar's line). The Idrisid vassal relations to Fatimids (al-Qasim Gannun for the Fatimids 938-948) and to the Umayyads (from 931 Musa; Hasan ibn Gannun in 954-974) are not entered as vassal events because the Idrisid page names the rulers, not the suzerain's boundary. Gazetteer names needed: Hajar an-Nasr (place, northern Morocco, rough point 35.17N 5.27W). Counterparts without a dossier: Banu Ifran of Tlemcen (Abu Qurra), the Miknasa of Fes (Masala ibn Habus, Musa ibn Abul 'Afiya). Rulers are not listed: the pages give Idris I 788-791, Idris II 803-828 and Muhammad 828-836 only. Method note: every page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model-made extraction; phrases in quotation marks are the extraction's wording of the page and may differ in small ways from the live text, while the years and months are the ones it reported.
